name: Thumbs Down
baseMeaning: A closed fist with the thumb pointing down — rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving.
tldr: The thumbs down emoji 👎 reads as rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving.

contextMeanings.meaning: In a dating thread the gesture is usually doing the work of a line that was not typed. It arrives as rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving, softened by whatever sentence sits next to it.

In a work channel it is read the same way it is read anywhere else — rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving — but the stakes of a misread are higher, because the sender is often talking about somebody's actual work.
The plain reading: a closed fist with the thumb pointing down. Nothing hidden in the drawing itself.
contextMeanings.example: Rating a restaurant or a pitch one star 👎

contextMeanings.meaning: Borrowed as a reaction, it reads as rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving.
contextMeanings.example: Quietly rejecting a plan in a group chat 👎

platformNotes.note: On Instagram 👎 usually arrives as the tail of a caption rather than as a post of its own — a sign-off that reads as rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving under a photo, or a reaction somebody left on a story.

In TikTok comments 👎 is the fastest way to answer a video without typing anything. The gesture stays rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving, and the tone of the comment underneath it carries the rest.

In Slack 👎 lands in channels where the sentence was supposed to be shorter. It is usually standing in for rating a restaurant or a pitch one star, and a channel where the topic is somebody's workload is where it misreads.
On Discord 👎 is a staple of the reaction bar, which is why it so often arrives stripped of its rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving reading — a shape pressed rather than a message sent.

On X and Twitter 👎 does most of its work in replies, where it tags a message like quietly rejecting a plan in a group chat. Short enough to survive being the whole post, which is exactly why it is used that way.

generationalNotes.note: Gen X mostly uses 👎 literally, as the picture of the gesture itself, and is less likely to read rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving into it than younger senders are.
Older senders use 👎 in the most straightforward way, on family and group messages, and are less likely to hear the rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving subtext in it.

Gen Z reaches for 👎 to do the work of rating a restaurant or a pitch one star, and treats the neutral drawing as the default rather than as a choice. What they hear first is rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving.

Millennials tend to send 👎 deliberately, usually for something like quietly rejecting a plan in a group chat, and they read rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving into it more often than the older cohorts do.

warnings.title: 👎 and 🖕 get swapped
warnings.description: The Middle Finger 🖕 is one tap away in every picker, and it does not carry the same reading — the middle finger aims at a person, the thumbs down aims at a thing. Check which one you actually picked.

warnings.title: The reading it usually gets is not the one it was sent with
warnings.description: People take 👎 as something else fairly often: it gets treated as a hard no or a personal attack when it is usually the mildest possible rating — a bare thumb carries no heat until a caption adds it. The sentence around it is usually what settles the meaning.

seoTitle: What Does the Thumbs Down Emoji 👎 Mean? A Full Breakdown
seoDescription: The meaning of 👎 Thumbs Down in texts and DMs, with the thumbs down readings, the common misread, and the pickers it gets confused with.

longForm.overview:
This page is the untoned drawing. Somewhere below it are five versions of the same thumbs down with a skin tone applied, and those pages are about something different: not what the gesture means, but what a particular tone adds to it when it arrives from a particular face.

The short version. The thumbs down is for rating a restaurant or a pitch one star and for quietly rejecting a plan in a group chat, it gets misread often enough to be worth writing down, and it has five skin-tone versions worth reading on their own. The sections below take those in turn.

Unicode 6.0 is where 👎 comes from. The drawing shows a closed fist with the thumb pointing down, it sits in the hands group of the set, and in a conversation it does one thing: it says what a sentence would have said less well.

What it says is rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving. That is the reading most people arrive with, and it is usually the intended one — the picture does the same work as the words it replaces, and it gets there faster.

The complication is that the drawing invites a second reading. It gets treated as a hard no or a personal attack when it is usually the mildest possible rating — a bare thumb carries no heat until a caption adds it. In practice that second reading is not rare — it is the one that decides how a message lands, because the sender has usually not thought about it at all.

It also sits in the crowded part of the picker. The nearest neighbour is 🖕 Middle Finger: the middle finger aims at a person, the thumbs down aims at a thing. The two are close enough that a fast thumb picks the wrong one, and the message goes out carrying a meaning nobody chose.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
There is one habit that turns a small emoji into a misunderstanding. 👎 goes back on its own, with no words around it, and it stands for whatever the sender had in mind — which was rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving. The reader gets the drawing and none of the context that produced it.

Start with Rating a restaurant or a pitch one star. That is where the thumbs down earns its place: it closes a sentence that has already said the thing, and nobody has to add "you know what I mean". The other job is quietly rejecting a plan in a group chat, and there the emoji is not the message but the temperature of the message.

The setting does half the work. 👎 used for rating a restaurant or a pitch one star in a work channel reads as a handover; the same move in a group chat reads as a joke. The emoji is not saying anything different — the audience is.

Which is also why this family has skin-tone pages. The gesture is the same in all five, and the tone you choose is the only part of the message that says anything about you.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
There is also a place where this emoji does not belong: the professional setting. 👎 under a review, or in a first message to a client, reads as rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving, and in that room the same reading sounds like somebody settling a point.

Two rules. First, 🖕 Middle Finger is a different message: the middle finger aims at a person, the thumbs down aims at a thing. Do not send 👎 when you meant that one. Second, a reaction to bad news needs words. A bare 👎 reads as rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving, and nobody in a thread about a person wants to be answered with a drawing of a gesture.

Not every message survives being turned into a picture. The emoji gets treated as a hard no or a personal attack when it is usually the mildest possible rating — a bare thumb carries no heat until a caption adds it, and the sentence underneath it loses the argument. Once 👎 is carrying the meaning, the meaning has moved without either sender moving it.

With somebody you have just met, it is worse. 👎 has no warmth in the drawing, and the gesture has picked up an edge of superiority from being used to answer other people.
longForm.howToReply:
If the intent is warmth, the sentence is the part that carries it. Sending 👎 next to a message like rating a restaurant or a pitch one star leaves the reader to guess whether it was rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving or something sharper.

If it was a reaction, 👎 back is a complete answer. It says "same" without writing a word, and the exchange can end there.

If it was aimed at you, it needs text. 👎 replying to 👎 looks like a conversation between two drawings, and whatever the sender actually asked never gets answered.

When the register is unclear, the words win. The drawing gets treated as a hard no or a personal attack when it is usually the mildest possible rating — a bare thumb carries no heat until a caption adds it, so the sentence it was sent with is the only reliable guide to what it meant.

faqs.question: Is 👎 rude?
faqs.answer: It can be. The gesture is meant as rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving, but it gets treated as a hard no or a personal attack when it is usually the mildest possible rating — a bare thumb carries no heat until a caption adds it. The risk is highest when it is the only message in the thread — a sentence gives the picture some context to sit in.

faqs.question: What does 👎 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: Nothing gender-specific. The same reading applies whoever sends it, and the meaning is set by the thread and by what is written next to it rather than by the sender.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 👎 and its skin-tone versions?
faqs.answer: The tone variants under thumbs down show the same gesture in five different skin tones. The gesture does not change, but the tone is a small signal about who the sender imagines the reader is, and in some groups that signal is read louder than the sentence.

faqs.question: What does 👎 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 👎 is used for rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving. The drawing shows a closed fist with the thumb pointing down, and that part is not in dispute — what changes is whether the sender is being literal or borrowing the gesture for a reaction.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 👎 and 🖕?
faqs.answer: The middle finger aims at a person, the thumbs down aims at a thing. The two sit close together in most pickers, so the difference is often about which one the sender pressed rather than about what they meant.

conversationExamples.interpretation: A small joke or a nudge, with the emoji doing the tone work. It gets treated as a hard no or a personal attack when it is usually the mildest possible rating — a bare thumb carries no heat until a caption adds it more easily here than it does in a work thread, because the thread is thinner.

conversationExamples.message: rating a restaurant or a pitch one star 👎
conversationExamples.interpretation: Family threads are where this lands most naturally. The reading is rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving, and nobody in the thread is reading it as anything sharper than that.
A public sign-off, with the emoji as the full stop. The picture is doing the punctuation, which is why it is sent instead of a sentence.

conversationExamples.message: rating a restaurant or a pitch one star 👎
conversationExamples.interpretation: The everyday use: the picture carries the whole line. It lands as rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving, and matching it with the same emoji is a normal reply.

conversationExamples.message: quietly rejecting a plan in a group chat 👎
conversationExamples.interpretation: A handover or a sign-off in a channel. It reads as rejecting, rating badly, or disapproving, and naming the next step in words is usually clearer than leaving it to the gesture.
